主要内容: On November 13, 2012, the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) released proposed recommendations for reforming money market mutual funds (MMFs) to address risks to the financial system. The Council, using its authority under Section 120 of the Dodd-Frank Act, proposed three alternatives for structural reforms. The first alternative requires MMFs to adopt a floating net asset value (NAV) by removing the exemption for amortized cost accounting and penny rounding. The second alternative introduces a stable NAV with a buffer of up to 1% and a minimum balance at risk (MBR) of 3% of shareholder balances over $100,000. The third alternative suggests a 3% NAV buffer combined with other measures like stricter diversification and liquidity requirements. The Council seeks public comment on these proposals and acknowledges the possibility of other reforms. The recommendations aim to reduce the risk of runs and enhance the resilience of MMFs. The Council emphasized that the reforms could increase demand for non-MMF cash management products. It also stated its intention to use its authorities to address any risks associated with a shift to non-MMF products. The proposed recommendations will undergo a 60-day public comment period, with comments submitted through regulations.gov. The Council also approved the minutes from its October 18, October 29, and October 30 meetings, which are available at fsoc.gov. The meeting participants included key financial regulators such as Treasury Secretary Tim Geithner, Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke, and others.
